items.title: Gucci La Famiglia: Marina Bay Sands launch recap
items.summary: Tatler Asia's writeup of Gucci's SS26 'La Famiglia' collection retail takeover at the Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands, one of only ten global cities carrying the line, continues to recirculate in regional fashion feeds; ambassador Billkin Putthipong and regional talents Haven, Zhang Ze Tong, Shye and Yang Yan attended, with the brand framing 'Gucciness' as a state of mind. Included as durable background context though the event itself is now roughly a year old; flagged as stale-event coverage rather than a fresh news hook.

items.title: Regional retail-trade coverage of Gucci's Kuala Lumpur boutique network
items.summary: Regional fashion trade coverage recaps Gucci's Kuala Lumpur footprint (now five Malaysian stores, four in KL including The Exchange TRX), circulated this week in retail commentary as a benchmark for how much Gucci is still investing in Malaysian mall-based retail even as APAC store counts contract elsewhere in the group.

items.title: Fan account event notice: Billkin at Gucci SS26 event Singapore
items.summary: Thai-fandom aggregator account posts an event-attendance notice for Billkin's appearance at the Gucci SS26 launch at Marina Bay Sands; representative of the ongoing fan-account tracking of the ambassador's brand appearances that keeps recirculating in SEA fan timelines. Old post, included only as an SNS-channel data point on fandom amplification behavior, not fresh news.

items.title: Why don't rich people buy Gucci anymore?
items.summary: Critical business-analysis piece argues Gucci is stuck between ultra-luxury and mass-accessible segments, citing weak new-product innovation, over-reliance on logos/prints, and a lack of quiet, high-end classic styles as reasons affluent shoppers across Asia-Pacific (including Southeast Asia) are turning to rivals; used this week in regional retail commentary to explain why Gucci's SEA growth lags peers like Hermes and Chanel among top-tier spenders.

items.source: Facebook (Gucci Philippines Buyers and Sellers group)
items.title: Philippine Gucci resale/preloved marketplace shows continued listing volume
items.summary: Recurring check of the active Philippine Facebook buy-sell-trade group for Gucci goods shows sustained listing volume for preloved/resale Gucci bags this week, a persistent community-level indicator of price-conscious secondary-market demand running parallel to official retail channels in the Philippines.

items.source: Weibo (cross-posted into SEA Chinese-diaspora shopping groups)
items.title: Discussion thread on Gucci's steep China price cuts (up to 40%) and whether Demna can revive the brand
items.summary: Chinese-language social discussion, reshared into Southeast Asian Chinese-diaspora shopping/resale groups in Singapore and Malaysia, analyzes Gucci's unusually steep September markdowns on bags like the Mercato tote (roughly 27% cut) and debates whether Demna's design direction can reverse the slide; regional resale-community members cite these China price cuts when discussing SEA cross-border purchasing arbitrage.

items.title: Kering Q2 2026 turnaround lifts shares 15.9 percent as Gucci sales decline slows
items.summary: Earnings-call coverage reports Kering shares jumped roughly 16% after Gucci's Q2 comparable sales fell only 2% (versus an expected ~3-4% decline), with CEO Luca de Meo's turnaround plan credited and 'all regions' cited as showing improved trends; referenced in this week's regional trade commentary (including the eu.36kr critical piece) as the financial backdrop against which SEA retail investment and store-closure decisions are being weighed. Included as background financial context; the event itself is outside the 14-day freshness window but remains the most recent group-level financial disclosure shaping regional coverage.

items.title: Kering closes 217 stores as Gucci sales plunge; nearly 40 percent of 2026 closures in Asian markets
items.summary: Business coverage reports Kering has closed 217 stores group-wide with more planned, noting close to 40% of 2026 closures fall in Asian markets (Japan plus wider Asia-Pacific, which includes Southeast Asian footprint); cited by commentators as evidence Gucci is retrenching from marginal Asian mall locations even while simultaneously opening flagship stores in top-tier SEA cities like Kuala Lumpur and Singapore.
